agent: Phase 3 Wave 1 Agent 3B (global edges + tensions synthesis)
scope: Volume-level canonical tensions across all 13 units of Calleja 2011 In-Game

tensions.label: PIM-as-structural-model vs experiential-phenomenology
tensions.description: Calleja constructs a six-dimensional structural model in Ch.3 with discrete categories, decomposition diagrams, and macro/micro temporal phasing — yet the phenomenon being modeled is preconscious, gestalt, lived involvement (Ch.10 'experiential gestalts' via Lakoff+Johnson). The Conclusion (Ch.11) explicitly anticipates a poststructural successor model, marking this tension as recognized by Calleja himself.
tensions.dissertation_implication: Justifies the dissertation's move to operationalize PIM as a *heuristic scaffold* rather than a rigid taxonomy; opens the door for Burke-pentad augmentation (Layer B) and Heidegger-BCAP temporal-phenomenology grounding (Layer A) as the poststructural successor Calleja gestures at but does not deliver.

tensions.label: Six-dimensions-discrete vs integrated-gestalt-incorporation
tensions.description: Ch.3 presents the six dimensions (kinesthetic / spatial / shared / narrative / affective / ludic) as analytically separable axes. Ch.10 then argues that *incorporation* is precisely the gestalt fusion of all six into a single non-decomposable experience. The model presupposes its own analytic violation: the dimensions are real only when described, while the experience is real only when unified.
tensions.dissertation_implication: Provides the dissertation's primary opening for cross-dimensional Burke-pentad ratios — pentad ratios are inherently multi-dimensional bridges. Also motivates the dissertation's Uexküll Funktionskreis augmentation (Layer C) since Funktionskreis is a single gestalt loop, not six separable channels.

tensions.label: Macro/micro-clean-split vs continuous-attention-gradient
tensions.description: Calleja repeatedly presents macro (off-line, anticipatory/retentional) and micro (in-session, moment-to-moment) phases as binary partitions. Yet his own examples — daydreaming about strategy mid-session, scheduling raid attendance during off-hours — show the phases bleeding into one another as a gradient of attentional pressure rather than two discrete modes.
tensions.dissertation_implication: Phantasia-Cluster bridge: anticipatory/retentional structure is a phantasia operation; the bleed itself is a Bowin-AMT continuous-motion phenomenon. The dissertation can argue the macro/micro split is heuristically useful but ontologically suspect, justifying replacement with kairic phasing from BCAP.

tensions.label: Murray-absorption-tradition vs presence-theory-displacement
tensions.description: Ch.2 critiques two pre-Calleja immersion lineages — Murray's absorption-into-narrative tradition and the Lombard/Ditton/Witmer/Singer presence-theory tradition — by pointing out their incompatible metaphors (transportation vs spatial-realism). Ch.10's incorporation move dissolves both, but at the cost of preserving Murray's experiential intuitions while jettisoning her vocabulary, and preserving presence-theory's spatial intuitions while jettisoning the here/there dichotomy.
tensions.dissertation_implication: Confirms the dissertation should NOT inherit Murray's transportation metaphor; positions incorporation (not presence) as the inheritable construct for Heidegger-BCAP in-der-Welt-sein bridging.

tensions.label: Lakoff-Johnson-naturalization vs residual phenomenological vocabulary
tensions.description: Ch.10 invokes Lakoff+Johnson 2003 'experiential gestalts' and Damasio 2000 on consciousness as Calleja's preferred grounding — a cognitivist-naturalist framework. Yet the descriptive vocabulary throughout the chapter ('experience', 'lived', 'inhabit', 'comportment') is unmistakably phenomenological, and the only Heidegger reference in the entire volume (p.21) is preserved as a sympathetic foothold. The naturalist scaffold cannot fully discharge the phenomenological residue.
tensions.dissertation_implication: Direct opening for the dissertation's Heidegger-BCAP Layer A: Calleja's phenomenological vocabulary is awaiting-ontological-grounding-in BCAP. The dissertation can argue that Lakoff+Johnson cannot fully ground the vocabulary Calleja uses, so a phenomenological-ontological supplement is required.

tensions.label: Three-not-four shared-subtypes typo / undercount
tensions.description: IG-06 Shared Involvement defines a micro-phase decomposition into 'cohabitation / cooperation / competition' (three subtypes) but the prose at p.93-97 enumerates a fourth — 'communication' or 'collaboration' depending on the passage — without integrating it into the figure-level diagram. The reader is left to reconcile a three-cell figure with a four-cell prose enumeration.
tensions.dissertation_implication: When operationalizing Shared involvement, the dissertation must elect either the three-subtype figure-level taxonomy or a four-subtype prose-level taxonomy and justify the choice. Recommend four-subtype with explicit acknowledgment of figure/prose mismatch.

tensions.label: Alterbiography occurs-in-micro-phase without labeled Micro-Phase subsection
tensions.description: IG-07 Narrative defines alterbiography (Calleja's signature term, p.115/124-125) as the emergent narrative co-produced by player + game in moment-to-moment play — clearly a micro-phase phenomenon. Yet Ch.7 lacks a clearly labeled 'Micro Phase' subsection paralleling Ch.4-6/8-9. The structural template breaks here.
tensions.dissertation_implication: Reinforces T-003: the macro/micro template is honored in the breach as well as the observance. The dissertation should treat alterbiography as a *kairic* narrative phenomenon (BCAP-grounded) rather than as a micro-phase narrative slot.

tensions.label: Atmospherics vs rules as primary affect-source
tensions.description: IG-08 Affective oscillates between two sources of in-game emotion: audiovisual atmospherics (lighting, score, environmental dread) on one side, and rule-induced stakes (failure penalties, time pressure, scarcity) on the other. Calleja does not adjudicate which is primary, and the chapter's brevity (12 pp., shortest dimension chapter) leaves the disjunct unresolved.
tensions.dissertation_implication: Strongest opening for the Gross 2017 Uncomfortable Situations bridge: situated-emotion theory adjudicates this by treating atmospherics-and-rules as a single affective situation. Also Uexküll Merktone/Wirktone bridge — environmental affect-tones and rule-induced effect-tones are both Funktionskreis components.

tensions.label: Mood/emotion conflation in Affective dimension
tensions.description: Ch.8 uses 'mood' (diffuse, sustained, non-intentional) and 'emotion' (acute, episodic, intentional) interchangeably across the chapter. Bryant+Davies 2006 and Grodal 2000 — the chapter's two principal interlocutors — themselves preserve the distinction, so the conflation is a Calleja-side flattening rather than an inherited one.
tensions.dissertation_implication: The dissertation should restore the mood/emotion distinction when operationalizing Affective involvement. Burke's pentad 'attitude' maps better to mood; 'purpose'-inflected emotion maps better to episodic affect.

tensions.label: Rules-as-constraint vs rules-as-meaningful-context
tensions.description: Ch.9 Ludic invokes Caillois (paidia/ludus) and Salen+Zimmerman to frame rules as constitutive constraints — what makes a game a game. But Calleja's own player-quotes describe rules as meaning-generators (mastery, fairness, expressive choice), not just constraints. The chapter does not reconcile rules-as-prohibition with rules-as-affordance.
tensions.dissertation_implication: Direct bridge to Bowin-AMT (motion-toward-end) and to Burke's purpose/agency ratio. Also surfaces the Gibsonian affordance reading Calleja avoids — the dissertation can argue rules are affordances-via-prohibition (Uexküll Funktionskreis tuning).

tensions.label: Ludic-agency vs narrative-determination
tensions.description: Ch.9 emphasizes meaningful player choice; Ch.7 emphasizes scripted-narrative pre-determination. The two dimensions are presented as analytically independent, yet every concrete example (quests, branching dialogue, mission failure) involves both simultaneously. The 'meaningful choice' celebrated in Ch.9 is constrained by the scripted-narrative architecture analyzed in Ch.7.
tensions.dissertation_implication: Alterbiography is precisely the construct that resolves this — it is the trace of ludic-agency exercised within narrative-determination. The dissertation should foreground alterbiography as the cross-dimensional integrator and (via Burke pentad) frame ludic/narrative as agency/scene+act ratio.

tensions.label: Habitation-as-trope vs designer-constituted bounded environment
tensions.description: IG-00 (Introduction), IG-05 (Spatial), and IG-10 (Incorporation) all invoke the 'metaphor of habitation' as the grounding image for incorporation. Yet game-worlds are not naturally inhabited the way Heideggerian dwellings are — they are designer-constituted, bounded, ruleful, and finite. Calleja uses habitation as both a phenomenological description (Ch.10) and a literary trope (Ch.5 'open landscape', Aarseth's labyrinth). The construct does not survive the transition cleanly.
tensions.dissertation_implication: Heidegger-BCAP Layer A: 'habitation' awaits-ontological-grounding-in In-der-Welt-sein, and the bounded-designer-world tension is precisely where Uexküll Umwelt (species-specific bounded environment) is a better fit than Heideggerian Welt. The dissertation can argue habitation should be re-grounded in Umwelt, not in Welt.

notes: Tensions T-001 through T-005 are dissertation-load-bearing — each directly motivates one of the three augmentation layers (Aristotle/Heidegger, Burke, Uexküll).
Tensions T-006, T-007 are editorial/structural defects in Calleja's text; the dissertation must elect a resolution when operationalizing those dimensions.
Tensions T-008, T-009 cluster on Ch.8 Affective — the chapter's brevity (12 pp.) is the proximate cause of both conflations.
Tension T-012 explicitly motivates the Uexküll-Umwelt repositioning that the cite-check (manifest.json) flagged as Layer C's required re-anchor after the Gibson-bridge falsification.

Candidate tensions deliberately omitted from this v1.0 list: (a) Place-vs-space (IG-05) — judged a productive elaboration rather than a tension; (b) WoW-cohabitation vs Planetside-competition (IG-APX) — judged a case-design asymmetry that supports rather than threatens the model. Both can be re-added as T-013/T-014 if downstream synthesis requires.
